title: mini-guardian: introduce mini-batcher guardian + quant telemetry adapter and CLI
author: Priya Kapoor
description: Motivation: Many production tenants see erratic micro-burst patterns where conservative batching settings either waste GPU cycles or cause tail-latency spikes. This PR introduces a lightweight 'mini-batcher guardian' runtime component that applies tenant-aware micro-batch shapes and a telemetry adapter that surfaces quantization sensitivity signals into our econ pipeline. It also adds a small CLI tool (quant-tuner) to synthesize candidate quant profiles from sampled workloads so tenants can safely evaluate compact quant profiles before rollout. Scope: runtime batching policy + guardian, telemetry bridge from runtime->econ service, quant-tuner CLI, docs and e2e smoke tests. Key behavior: - Mini-batcher guardian maintains per-tenant microburst counters and decides when to force smaller batch shapes for latency SLOs or larger shapes for cost SLOs. Decisions are policy-driven and respect tenant overrides. - Telemetry adapter exports a new signal stream: quant_sensitivity_{tenant,model,window} (estimated loss/cost delta for candidate quant tiers) and mini_batch_shape_{tenant,window}. These appear in the econ pipeline and console. - quant-tuner CLI can ingest replay/sampled traces and output N candidate quant profiles with safety estimates (expected token-cost delta, rank-regression estimate). Implementation notes: The guardian is intentionally minimal and runs as a hot-path filter inside the serving runtime; careful attention paid to allocation-free path for the common case. Quant-tuner is a standalone binary (go) that reuses model sampling and offline evaluator components. Backward compatibility: runtime flags default to off; admin-enabled per-cluster via feature flag enable_mini_guardian=true. Rollout plan: staged behind feature flag for 10 internal tenants -> 40 canaries -> global after 2 weeks of telemetry. Tests & results: microbench in perf-lab with sample multi-tenant chat workload (70/30 short/long tokens) shows median latency change: +0.6% (statistically neutral) and p95 latency down 4.1% for bursty tenants; token unit cost reduction ~7.8% for cost-optimized profiles when quant-tuner profiles used. Risks/mitigation: false-positive quant regressions — quant-tuner outputs conservative regression scores and PR includes automatic fallback to baseline model variant. What changed (high level): - runtime/mini_guardian.*: guardian logic and policy engine - runtime/batcher/*: new small batch shaper and containerized tests - telemetry/adapters/quant_telemetry.go: new adapter and export plumbing - tools/quant-tuner/: CLI, samplers, and offline evaluator - docs/ops/mini-guardian.md: rollout + feature flags - tests/e2e/mini_guardian_smoke_test.py: smoke + perf checks This description is a single continuous string and includes checklists, test summary and rollout notes.

release_notes:
- Add mini-batcher guardian to allow tenant-aware micro-batch shaping (feature-flag gated).
- Export quant sensitivity telemetry to econ pipeline (quant_v1 signals).
- Add quant-tuner CLI to generate candidate quant profiles from sampled traces (experimental).
- Minor docs and an e2e smoke test for guardian + quant flow.
merge_summary: Merged after requested changes were addressed. Rollout behind feature flag; initial internal canary scheduled.
qa_notes: Smoke tests included: unit tests, a quant-tuner sample run, and a perf-lab integration harness. Ops should enable feature flag and watch telemetry dashboard: quant_sensitivity_* and mini_batch_shape_* before broad rollout. If quant_sensitivity shows sustained negative regression >0.5% on eval set, auto-disable rollout for that tenant.
